2027-05-07.title: Sixth Friday of Resurrection · First Friday
2027-05-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The one who comes from above is above all
2027-05-07.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The day after the Ascension of our Lord, and the First Friday of the month, kept with devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Many begin today the novena to the Holy Spirit, the nine days of prayer that lead to Pentecost.
2027-05-07.verse: He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
theo: Yesterday the Church celebrated the Ascension of our Lord. The disciples stood on the Mount of Olives looking up, and two men in white asked them, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” (Acts 1:11). Then they went back to Jerusalem, to the upper room, and began to pray. Today's Gospel is a commentary on what they had just seen. “The one who comes from above is above all; the one who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is above all.” These words, at the end of the third chapter of John, describe Jesus as the One who came down from the Father; after the Ascension we hear them also as a description of the One who has gone back up. He came from above, and he has returned above. He is not one teacher among many, not a holy man who rose a little higher than the rest of us: he is the One who is above all. That is why the Church can call him Lord, and why the Holy Qurbana is offered to him and through him to the Father. The Gospel adds a sad line: “yet no one accepts his testimony.” But it also adds a promise: “Whoever has accepted his testimony has certified this, that God is true.” Every act of faith is a little seal pressed on the truth of God.

Then comes the verse that opens the nine days before Pentecost: “He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.” The prophets received the Spirit for a time and for a task. The Son receives the Spirit without measure, and he gives the Spirit without measure. Before he went to the Father he had promised, “if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you” (John 16:7). The Ascension is not an absence; it is the condition of the gift. So the disciples do not sit idle in the upper room. They pray, “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). The Church has always seen in those days the first novena, nine days of prayer with the Mother of the Lord, waiting for the Spirit who would make them a Church. The Gospel closes with the Father's love: “The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.” The hands that were nailed to the Cross now hold all things. On this First Friday we look also at the pierced side of the same Lord: from his open Heart came blood and water (John 19:34), and from that Heart the Spirit is poured out.

Paul writes to the Philippians as a man who has met that Lord and cannot stand still. “Not that I have already obtained this or have already reached the goal; but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own.” Paul does not boast of what he has reached. He speaks like a runner in the last lap: “forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.” The Greek words behind “the heavenly call” can mean “the upward call”: God calls us upward, where Christ has gone before us. The Ascension gives our whole life a direction. We do not run in circles; we run toward the place where our Head has already arrived. And Paul adds a gentle word for those who see things differently: “if you think differently about anything, this too God will reveal to you.” The one who runs toward Christ is patient with fellow runners. The novena begins today: let it be nine days of running toward the Lord, forgetting the failures behind us, and asking the Father for the Spirit who is given without measure.
conn: Why do you stand looking up?
At the Ascension the two men in white said, “This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven” (Acts 1:11).
“Out of the believer's heart shall flow rivers of living water.” John adds: “as yet there was no Spirit, because Jesus was not yet glorified” (John 7:38–39).
“One of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out” (John 19:34); the Church sees here the birth of the sacraments from the Heart of Christ.
“All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14).
“Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary” (Isaiah 40:31).
“So if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God” (Colossians 3:1).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lord who has gone up to the Father comes down to us in his Body and Blood. He is above all, and yet he lets himself be held in our hands. From the altar, as from his pierced Heart, flow the blood and water of the sacraments.

On this First Friday many receive Holy Communion in reparation and love, as the Lord asked through St Margaret Mary. Receive him today with a heart that is straining forward, asking him for the Spirit.
outline: The day after the Ascension: disciples who stop looking up and start praying.
Point 1 · The One from above is above all
The Ascended Lord, his testimony, and our seal on the truth of God.
Point 2 · He gives the Spirit without measure
The first novena, with Mary in the upper room, and the open Heart of Jesus.
Point 3 · I press on toward the goal
The upward call: the Ascension gives our life a direction.
A relay runner who forgets the stumble on the first bend and runs toward the hand stretched out at the finish.
live: Pray each day until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.” Pray it with Mary, asking her to pray with you.
Go to confession and receive Holy Communion today if you can, and spend a few minutes before the Sacred Heart.
Name one failure you keep returning to, place it in the Heart of Jesus, and decide not to carry it into these nine days.
Read one page of the Gospel slowly today and say at the end: Lord, I believe that you speak the words of God.
fathers: Christ has ascended into heaven: let our hearts ascend with him. He is there, and yet he is still with us here; we are here, and yet we are already with him there. He by his divinity, his power and his love; we by love, though not yet in body.

Paul, who had been caught up to the third heaven, still says that he strains forward. To find God is to go on seeking him; the desire for God is never filled up and ended, because God has no limit. The soul that loves him always rises higher.
magis: The Ascension marks the definitive entrance of Jesus' humanity into God's heavenly domain. As Head of the Church he precedes us, so that we, his members, may live in the hope of one day being with him for ever; there he intercedes for us.
Only when the hour has arrived for his glorification does Jesus promise the coming of the Holy Spirit, since his death and Resurrection will fulfil the promise made to the fathers.
After her Son's Ascension, Mary aided the beginnings of the Church by her prayers: with the apostles and the women, she implored by her prayers the gift of the Spirit.

Jesus knew and loved us each and all during his life, his agony and his Passion, and gave himself up for each one of us. The Sacred Heart of Jesus, pierced by our sins and for our salvation, is the chief sign and symbol of that love.
saints: 7–13 May: the days after the Ascension of our Lord (Thursday 6 May), when the apostles waited in prayer for the Holy Spirit “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Many families and parishes pray a novena to the Holy Spirit from Friday 7 to Saturday 15 May, the eve of Pentecost. Fri 7: First Friday. Sun 9: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension; the Latin Church in India celebrates the Ascension on this Sunday. Mon 10: in the Latin calendar, St John of Avila. Wed 12: in the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras. Thu 13: in the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima. The Marian month of May continues (verify locally).
2027-05-07.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came from above and you have returned to the Father; you are above all, and all things are placed in your hands. As your disciples waited in the upper room with Mary your Mother, we wait for the Spirit whom you give without measure. Open the treasures of your Sacred Heart to us on this First Friday; make us forget what lies behind and run toward the upward call of God. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be glory for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: The day after the Ascension: the One who comes from above is above all.
He gives the Spirit without measure: the nine days of prayer for Pentecost begin.
Paul: forgetting what lies behind, I press on toward the goal of the upward call of God.
2027-05-07.action: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit today, and pray it with Mary for nine days.
2027-05-07.question: Am I standing still, looking at what lies behind, or straining forward toward the Lord who has gone ahead?
catechism: Mary prays with the apostles for the Spirit.
kidsaint: Margaret Mary was a sister in a convent at Paray-le-Monial in France. In the 1670s, while she prayed before the Blessed Sacrament, Jesus showed her his Heart burning with love for people. He asked that people receive Holy Communion on the First Friday of the month to love him and to make up for the times he is forgotten. That is why many families go to Holy Qurbana on First Fridays! Lesson: Jesus' Heart is full of love for you; you can love him back.
2027-05-07.special: Sixth Friday of Resurrection. First Friday. The day after the Ascension (Thursday 6 May); the novena to the Holy Spirit begins.
term: Nine days of prayer for one intention, from the Latin novem, ‘nine’. The Church sees the first novena in the nine days between the Ascension and Pentecost, when the apostles prayed together with Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14) and received the Holy Spirit. The novena to the Holy Spirit, prayed from the Friday after the Ascension to the eve of Pentecost, keeps that pattern.

family.explain: Yesterday we remembered how Jesus went up to heaven. Before he went, he promised to send the Holy Spirit. So the disciples went into a room in Jerusalem and prayed with Mary, Jesus' mother, for nine days. Today the Gospel says that God gives the Spirit ‘without measure’: not a little cup, but a whole river! For nine days we too can pray with Mary: Come, Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that the Holy Spirit may fill our home with love and peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift do we want the Holy Spirit to give our family at Pentecost?” Write it on a paper and keep it near the family altar until Pentecost.

illus: At a school sports day in Thrissur, a girl running the third leg of the relay slipped on the first bend and fell. Her knee was bleeding and her team was suddenly last. She could have sat on the track and cried over the fall. Instead she got up, forgot the bend behind her and ran with all her strength toward the next runner, who was standing with her hand stretched back. The team did not win, but the whole ground stood up and clapped as she passed the baton. Paul says that the Christian life is like that: forgetting what lies behind, we run toward the hand stretched out to us, the hand of the Lord who has gone ahead.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have gone up to the Father and you give the Spirit without measure. As we begin these nine days, gather us with Mary your Mother in prayer, and pour out your Spirit on us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: The one who comes from above is above all (John 3:31). Is Jesus truly above all in my life, or is he one concern among many?
He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). What do I most need to ask from the Holy Spirit in this novena?
Forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead (Philippians 3:13). What past failure or hurt do I keep carrying?
They were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). How can our group pray together until Pentecost?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.
interc: For the Church, gathered in prayer as in the upper room, that she may receive the Spirit anew at Pentecost.
For our Syro-Malabar Church, our bishops, priests and religious, that the Spirit may renew their zeal.
For those who are tired and have stopped running, that the Lord may lift them up and set their face toward the goal.
For those who keep the First Friday today, that the Heart of Jesus may heal and strengthen them.
For our families, that we may pray together with Mary in these nine days.
pm.close: Father, your Son has gone up to you and has placed all things in your hands. Through his pierced Heart, pour out on us the Spirit without measure, that we may run toward the upward call you have given us in Christ Jesus our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated the Ascension of our Lord. The disciples watched him go up, and then they went back to Jerusalem, to the upper room, to pray. Today we begin to pray with them.

The Gospel says: “The one who comes from above is above all.” Jesus came from the Father, and now he has returned to the Father. He is not one good teacher among many. He is above all. And “the Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.” The hands that were nailed to the Cross now hold the whole world, and they hold each of us.

Then comes a beautiful line: “he gives the Spirit without measure.” Jesus had said, if I go, I will send the Advocate to you. So the Ascension is not a goodbye; it is the beginning of a gift. For nine days the apostles prayed with Mary, the mother of Jesus, waiting for that gift. This was the first novena of the Church. Let us pray it with them until Pentecost.

Today is also the First Friday. We look at the Heart of Jesus, pierced on the Cross, from which came blood and water. From that open Heart the Spirit is poured out on the Church. Let us come to confession, receive him in the Holy Qurbana, and ask his Heart for the gift of the Spirit.

And Paul tells us how to live these days: “forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal.” God's call is an upward call: where Christ has gone, we are called to follow. Let us not sit down on the track and cry over yesterday's fall. Let us get up and run toward him. Come, Holy Spirit! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, yesterday Jesus went up to heaven. But he did not leave us alone! He promised to send the Holy Spirit.
For nine days the disciples prayed with Mary, waiting for the Holy Spirit. Can you pray with them? Every day until Pentecost, say: ‘Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart!’

The day after the Ascension and the first day of the novena: the Lord above all, the Spirit poured out from his open Heart, and the upward call that sets our life in motion.

points.h: He gives the Spirit without measure

Nine days with Mary in the upper room.
From the pierced Heart, rivers of living water.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.

sub: The upward call of God in Christ Jesus.

concl: The Lord who has gone up is above all, and from his open Heart he gives the Spirit without measure.
With Mary in the upper room, let us pray, forget what lies behind and run toward the upward call.
2027-05-07.resolve: For these nine days, pray daily with Mary for the Holy Spirit, and let one old failure go into the Heart of Jesus.
